items.stem: For a stable patient with a well-controlled chronic condition who reports worsening symptoms, the best first step is to:

options.text: Reassess adherence and contributing factors before escalating therapy
options.rationale: Correct: reassessing adherence and triggers precedes intensifying treatment.
Escalation without reassessment may mask the real cause.
Stopping effective therapy is not justified.
Surgery is not indicated from the information given.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate when managing an acute, undifferentiated presentation?

options.text: Use pretest probability to guide testing
options.rationale: Correct: pretest probability focuses the work-up efficiently.

options.text: Order every available test at once
options.rationale: Indiscriminate testing increases false positives and cost.

options.text: Delay all treatment until a final diagnosis
options.rationale: Treatment of immediate threats should not wait for a final diagnosis.

options.text: Rely only on the patient's self-diagnosis
options.rationale: Self-diagnosis is not a substitute for clinical assessment.
